name: CompoundUnits
summary: Builds a unit out of other units raised to powers, so that a rate, an area or a dose per kilogram is a unit the model can reason about rather than a string.

roles.name: Unit
roles.summary: What a quantity is measured in, atomic or compound indifferently. The role sits on the supertype because that is the point: a quantity holds a unit without caring which kind it is, and a conversion between millilitres per hour and litres per day is asked of the same interface as one between grams and kilograms.

roles.name: AtomicUnit
roles.summary: A unit that decomposes no further — a metre, a gram, a second.

roles.name: CompoundUnit
roles.summary: A unit made of unit references. Figure 3.4 states the constraint that keeps it from being a redundant wrapper: it must hold more than one reference, or one whose power is negative or above one. A compound unit of a single reference to the power of one is a metre spelled twice.

roles.name: UnitReference
roles.summary: One unit and the power it is raised to. The power is what makes the model reason rather than concatenate: metres to the power of two is an area and metres to the power of minus one is a reciprocal, and a name like "m2" says neither to anything.
